concerns.text: The validation of substructure attribution (SC-005) relies on matching the top‑20 substructures—defined as *contiguous aromatic or conjugated fragments* (FR‑006 aggregation rule)—against a curated reference set of fluorophore motifs (FR‑016). Because the reference motifs are themselves largely characterized by aromatic/conjugated fragments, the validation target is not truly independent of the predictor: any method that aggregates attributions into such fragments will inevitably achieve high overlap, making the ≥60 % overlap criterion potentially tautological. This circular relationship undermines the claim that the attribution analysis provides a scientifically meaningful test of model interpretability.

FR‑012 specifies detection and logging of unseen atom/bond types, with different handling for inference versus test‑set evaluation, but the specification provides no independent test or validation scenario for this behavior. Without a defined test (e.g., a dataset containing deliberately novel atom types) the requirement cannot be empirically verified, leaving a methodological gap in the validation of the pipeline’s robustness to out‑of‑distribution chemistry.
